chapter_title_en: The Rusty Knife and the Forgotten Hand
chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 354: The Heart-Turbid Strikes at Memory
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang hunts a Heart-Turbid with a bizarre task force, but the real attack isn't claws—it's a memory so cleanly erased he forgets the knife in his own hand.
og_title: The Rusty Knife and the Forgotten Hand – Dao Gui Yi Xian Chapter 354
og_description: A hunt for a memory-stealing monster turns inward when Li Huowang forgets why he’s holding a weapon.
twitter_title: “Where did this knife come from?” The heart-turbid hits Li Huowang where it hurts—his mind.
twitter_description: This chapter’s horror isn’t a monster—it’s a perfect, clean hole in memory.

lore_anchors.definition: A new type of entity distinct from the Heart-Element (心素). It appears to be a parasitic or reality-distorting monster that targets perception and memory. The name implies a corruption of the heart-mind, making it a “turbid” or impure presence in the world.

A high-ranking eunuch official in the Supervisory Heavenly Office; their power is both bureaucratic and supernatural, often wielded through a deceptively genial demeanor. Here, he leads the hunt for the Heart-Turbid.
A traditional northeastern Chinese spirit-summoning verse, used by chuma spirit mediums. Shen Tugang’s version is notably more aggressive and powerful than earlier examples in the story.
The assistant in a spirit-dance ritual. Often silent and puppet-like, but capable of independent action. In this chapter, she has been following Li Huowang, referring to herself as his wife.

A handler in the Supervisory Heavenly Office; his compound surname (Tuoba) marks him as being from a historical non-Han ruling clan, adding cultural depth. He is sycophantic toward the Chief Recorder but seems to be probing Li Huowang.
